_comment: Antigravity (`agy`) static tool policy — the sandbox-owned half of /root/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json. SEEDED AND MERGED by scripts/profile.sh on every `up`: only the two keys in this file are written, every other key agy stores there (colorScheme, model, trustedWorkspaces, enableTelemetry) is preserved. Convergence runs on every `up`/`recreate`/`rebuild`/`wipe`; `scripts/profile.sh <profile> converge` runs the same thing without touching containers (the three reset-* commands it replaced were removed in work/0011). Restart `agy` inside the container to pick it up. See sandbox_templates/antigravity/README.md and docs/adr/0006-antigravity-is-two-layer-like-claude.md.
_comment_parity: Mirrors permissions.allow/ask/deny in ../claude/claude-settings.json, converted from Claude's `Bash(x:*)` matcher to agy's `command(x)` grant. BOTH matchers are PREFIX matchers over the command line, so the conversion is one-to-one and the two agents deny the same set. scripts/agent-policy.test.sh fails if they ever diverge — that suite is the anti-drift control, so add a command to BOTH files or to neither.
_comment_deny_is_the_tamper_resistant_la: The hard denials live HERE rather than in the PreToolUse hook because a workspace .agents/hooks.json can disable the hook by name (measured — work/0010 Phase 0, test G), and nothing in a workspace can reach settings.json. The hook is defence-in-depth on top of this list, not a substitute for it.
_comment_ask_cache: agy caches an `ask` approval as an Always-Allow grant, so an entry in the `ask` list below prompts ONCE, unlike Claude's permissions.ask which re-prompts. Since work/0004 the shared hook engine DOES emit `force_ask` (agy's own enum value, documented in the shipped binary as 'Always prompt the user, ignoring cached permissions') — but only for the DELETION verbs it added a rule for: git rm, the worktree-discarding git checkout/restore forms, git stash drop/clear, git branch -d/-D, unlink, and plain rm outside the disposable-path carve-outs. The eight mutating myclickup writes listed below are NOT yet re-asserted that way and remain cache-backed: one approval makes each permanent for the profile. Wiring them through force_ask is named as follow-up in work/0004 (Future scope 1). An earlier version of this comment claimed the hook already did this for the myclickup set; it did not, and the hook contained no force_ask at all — the claim was aspirational and is corrected here.
_comment_toolPermission: request-review is already agy's default. Pinning it means a future change to that default, or an accidental `always-proceed`, does not silently widen the profile. Other values: strict, always-proceed, proceed-in-sandbox.

permissions._comment_allow: Read-only inspection, the safe git verbs, project-local build/test runners, the myclickup read subcommands, and the three myclickup writes promoted on 2026-08-24 (comment/set-status/update — see _comment_ask). Prefix matching: command(ls) covers `ls -la /x`.
permissions._comment_paperbridge: The 30 paperbridge entries mirror claude-settings.json exactly — same 20 allow / 8 ask / 2 deny, translated Bash(x:*) -> command(x), which is the ONLY difference between the two grammars. The twin is not optional: scripts/agent-policy.test.sh diffs both lists in BOTH directions for allow/ask/deny alike with no exception list, so a one-sided edit fails offline before docker is involved. Read out of the depot manifest at 0.2.1, never retyped. Owner decision 2026-09-09 (work/0026 D4). THE agy-SPECIFIC PART: agy caches an `ask` approval as a permanent Always-Allow grant, so every one of these 8 writes is one prompt away from permanent here — unlike claude, where `ask` re-prompts. `zotero-delete` is the exception and is deliberately not left to this list: it carries a force_ask rule in the shared hook engine (work/0026 D5), so it prompts every time regardless of the cache. The other seven remain cache-backed, exactly as the eight myclickup writes above do; wiring those through force_ask is still the open follow-up named in work/0004. `download` and `export` sit in `allow` and write files unprompted — fenced by the tool's own 12-host download allowlist, not by this file; see the claude note.
permissions._comment_ask: Mutating myclickup subcommands — a write to a real ClickUp workspace is the user's call, not the agent's. THREE writes are deliberately ABSENT from this list and sit in `allow` instead — comment, set-status and update, promoted by explicit owner sign-off on 2026-08-24 (work/0011 T00, spec F7). The twin promotion in claude-settings.json is not optional: scripts/agent-policy.test.sh diffs the two grammars exactly in BOTH directions for allow and ask alike, so a one-sided edit fails offline. Note agy caches an `ask` approval as an Always-Allow grant, so for agy these three were already one prompt away from permanent; the promotion makes that explicit and reviewable in the template rather than implicit in a cache.
permissions._comment_deny: Network tools, remote VCS, every package installer and fetch-and-run form, shell escapes and interpreter one-liners, and the destructive primitives. Reads of secret FILES are not expressible as a command() grant and are enforced by the hook instead (rule cred-read), which sees view_file, grep_search and run_command alike.
